business_problem: After launching more than 40 generative AI experiments, Sun Life needed to move from experimentation to production value with a secure way for employees to retrieve internal information quickly inside the company’s own technology environment.
solution_summary: Sun Life turned its early generative AI experiments into a production knowledge assistant by building Sun Life Asks on AWS. The chatbot runs inside the company’s secure technology environment and uses Amazon Bedrock to access Anthropic Claude models without Sun Life having to manage model infrastructure. Employee questions are grounded in internal company information, processed by Bedrock, and returned through the Sun Life Asks interface to staff across global operations. This architecture let Sun Life move from experimentation to value delivery quickly while keeping governance inside its own environment, and it created a reusable pattern for future client-facing use cases as the company scales broader generative AI adoption and workforce upskilling.

solution_components.name: Amazon Bedrock
solution_components.role: Provides the foundation-model service Sun Life uses to run its internal Sun Life Asks chatbot.

data_flow: Employee questions and internal company information flow into Sun Life Asks, which uses Amazon Bedrock and Anthropic Claude to generate secure responses for employees across Sun Life’s global operations.
integration_points: internal information used by Sun Life Asks
business_outcome: Sun Life Asks is handling more than 10,000 employee queries each week, resolved more than 600,000 internal queries in its first 11 months, and saves team members hours of manual work so they can reinvest time in higher-value tasks while Sun Life prepares additional client-facing AI use cases.
